cashTip: Cards work in hotels and malls; carry shillings for markets, bajajis and street food. US dollars are handy for visas and some tours.
name: Dar es Salaam
tagline: Tanzania's lively harbour city and gateway to Zanzibar
summary: Dar es Salaam is Tanzania's biggest city, a busy Indian Ocean port mixing Swahili, Arab, Indian and German heritage. Wander the huge Kariakoo Market, watch the morning auction at the Kivukoni fish market, see Makonde carvings at Mwenge, snorkel off Bongoyo Island and eat mishkaki skewers at Coco Beach before the ferry to Zanzibar.
seasonNote: June to October is dry and cooler; long rains fall March to May.
arrival: Julius Nyerere International is 30 to 60 minutes from the centre depending on traffic.
gettingAround: Uber, Bolt and bajajis; the BRT bus is quick on its lanes.
foodTip: Mishkaki, chips mayai, pilau and fresh seafood.
buyTip: Tingatinga paintings, Makonde carvings and kanga cloth.
baseArea: City Centre, Masaki or Oyster Bay

connections.note: Fast ferries several times a day.

items.name: Kariakoo Market
items.summary: East Africa's busiest market, spilling across dozens of streets.
items.tip: Go with a local guide in the morning.

items.name: Kivukoni Fish Market
items.summary: Dhows unload the catch and auctioneers sell it on the beach.
items.tip: Arrive by 7 a.m. for the auction.

items.name: National Museum
items.summary: Fossils from Olduvai Gorge and Swahili coast history.
items.tip: Pair with the botanical garden next door.

items.name: Bongoyo Island
items.summary: Boat trip to an uninhabited island with beaches and snorkelling.
items.tip: Bring cash for grilled fish on the beach.

items.name: Village Museum
items.summary: Open-air museum of traditional houses from Tanzania's tribes.

items.name: Mwenge Carvers Market
items.summary: Workshops where Makonde carvers make ebony sculptures.

items.name: Askari Monument and old town
items.summary: Bronze WWI memorial and nearby German and Indian-era buildings.

items.name: Coco Beach mishkaki
items.summary: Evening grills of beef mishkaki and cassava by the sea.

items.name: Chips mayai
items.summary: Chips cooked into an omelette, Tanzania's favourite street food.

items.name: Swahili seafood
items.summary: Coconut fish curry, pilau and octopus.

cashTip: Uganda uses the shilling (about 3,700 to 1 US dollar); prices here are in US dollars. Gorilla permits and lodges are priced in dollars; carry shillings for boda-bodas and markets.
name: Kampala
tagline: Hilly capital, base for the Nile and mountain gorillas
summary: Kampala is Uganda's buzzing capital, spread over green hills by Lake Victoria. Visit the royal Kasubi Tombs and the minaret of the Gaddafi Mosque, see the Uganda Martyrs Shrine at Namugongo, eat a rolex from a street stand, raft the Nile at Jinja, and set off for gorilla trekking in Bwindi.
seasonNote: June to August and December to February are the drier seasons, best for gorilla treks.
arrival: Entebbe International is about 45 minutes to an hour by the expressway.
gettingAround: SafeBoda and Uber; boda-bodas are fast but wear a helmet.
foodTip: Rolex, luwombo, matooke and Nile tilapia.
buyTip: Bark cloth, baskets and crafts at the National Theatre craft market.

items.name: Kasubi Tombs
items.wiki: Tombs of Buganda Kings at Kasubi
items.summary: UNESCO-listed thatched royal tombs of the Buganda kings.

items.name: Gaddafi National Mosque
items.summary: Large mosque whose minaret gives the best view over the city.

items.name: Uganda Martyrs Shrine Namugongo
items.summary: Basilica where Christian converts were martyred in 1886; huge pilgrimage on 3 June.
items.tip: Visit the lake and Anglican shrine too.

items.name: Uganda Museum
items.summary: East Africa's oldest museum of ethnography and music.

items.name: Source of the Nile at Jinja
items.summary: Where the White Nile leaves Lake Victoria; rafting, kayaking and boat trips.

items.name: Entebbe and Lake Victoria
items.summary: Botanical gardens, wildlife centre and lake beaches.
items.tip: Good on arrival or departure day.

items.name: Bwindi gorilla trekking
items.summary: Trek through rainforest to spend an hour with mountain gorillas.
items.expect: Permits cost about 800 USD and sell out.
items.tip: Book permits months ahead; fly to Kihihi.

items.name: Rolex street food
items.summary: Chapati rolled with an omelette and vegetables.

items.name: Luwombo and matooke
items.summary: Stew steamed in banana leaves with mashed plantain.

items.name: Lakeside tilapia at Ggaba
items.summary: Whole fried Nile tilapia at Lake Victoria landing.

cashTip: Madagascar uses the ariary (about 5,000 to 1 euro); prices here are in euros. Cash is king outside hotels; ATMs work in Tana but are scarce elsewhere.
name: Antananarivo
tagline: Hilltop capital and launchpad for lemurs and baobabs
summary: Antananarivo, or Tana, is Madagascar's capital, a jumble of red-brick houses on twelve hills. See the Rova royal palace above the city, visit the sacred hill of Ambohimanga, meet lemurs at Lemurs' Park, and set out for the rainforest of Andasibe or the famous Avenue of the Baobabs.
seasonNote: April to November is dry; December to March is cyclone and rainy season.
arrival: Ivato International is 30 to 60 minutes from the centre.
gettingAround: Taxis by agreement or a car with driver; traffic is heavy.
foodTip: Romazava, zebu brochettes, mofo gasy and vanilla everything.
buyTip: Vanilla, raffia crafts and embroidery at the Digue market.

items.name: Rova of Antananarivo
items.summary: Restored royal palace on the city's highest hill.
items.tip: Late afternoon light over the city.

items.name: Royal Hill of Ambohimanga
items.summary: UNESCO sacred hill and fortified royal village.

items.name: Lemurs' Park
items.summary: Free-roaming lemurs in a rescue park.

items.name: Andasibe-Mantadia
items.summary: Rainforest home of the singing indri lemur.
items.tip: Do a night walk for chameleons.

items.name: Avenue of the Baobabs
items.summary: Giant baobab trees lining a dirt road at sunset.

items.name: Analakely market
items.summary: Busy central market under white umbrellas.

items.name: Lake Anosy
items.summary: Heart-shaped lake with jacaranda blooms in October.

items.name: Romazava
items.summary: Beef and leafy greens stew, the national dish.

items.name: Mofo gasy
items.summary: Sweet rice cakes from street stalls.

items.name: Zebu brochettes
items.summary: Grilled zebu skewers and steaks.

cashTip: Cards and Pix work almost everywhere; carry a little cash for markets and boat trips.
name: Manaus
tagline: Opera house city in the heart of the Amazon
summary: Manaus is a rubber-boom city deep in the Amazon, the gateway for jungle lodges and river trips. See the pink-domed Teatro Amazonas, watch the dark Rio Negro meet the sandy Solimões without mixing, climb the canopy tower at MUSA, and head upriver to the Anavilhanas islands and pink river dolphins.
seasonNote: July to November is the drier season with beaches; high water from April to June floods the forest.
arrival: Eduardo Gomes International is 30 minutes from the centre.
gettingAround: Uber in the city; boats and tours for the river.
foodTip: Tambaqui, tacacá soup and the x-caboquinho sandwich.
baseArea: Centro near the theatre or Ponta Negra

items.name: Teatro Amazonas
items.summary: 1896 opera house with a dome of Brazilian-flag tiles.
items.expect: Tours paid; free concerts some nights.

items.name: Meeting of the Waters
items.summary: Dark Rio Negro and pale Solimões run side by side for kilometres.

items.name: MUSA canopy tower
items.summary: Forest reserve with a 42-metre tower above the canopy.

items.name: Anavilhanas and pink dolphins
items.summary: Flooded island maze and swimming with boto dolphins.

items.name: Adolpho Lisboa Market
items.summary: Iron market modelled on Les Halles, selling fish and herbs.

items.name: Ponta Negra beach
items.summary: River beach with sunset promenade.

items.name: Grilled tambaqui
items.summary: Rib of giant river fish grilled over coals.

items.name: Tacacá
items.summary: Hot soup of tucupi, jambu leaves and shrimp that numbs the lips.
items.tip: Buy from street stalls by the theatre.

items.name: X-caboquinho
items.summary: Roll with tucumã palm fruit and coalho cheese.

cashTip: Carry soles; cards work in town restaurants but trekking agencies and colectivos want cash.
name: Huaraz
tagline: Trekking capital under the Cordillera Blanca
summary: Huaraz is Peru's trekking capital, a high Andean town beneath the glaciers of the Cordillera Blanca. Hike to the turquoise Laguna 69, see the Llanganuco lakes under Huascarán, visit the 3,000-year-old temple of Chavín de Huántar and touch the Pastoruri glacier.
seasonNote: May to September is dry with clear skies; acclimatise for two days before high hikes.
arrival: Overnight buses from Lima take about 8 hours; small flights land at Anta airport.
gettingAround: Colectivos and tour vans; taxis in town.
foodTip: Pachamanca, picante de cuy and trout.

items.name: Laguna 69
items.summary: Turquoise lake under glaciers at 4,600 metres; tough 14 km hike.
items.why: The best day hike in Peru.

items.name: Llanganuco lakes
items.summary: Emerald lakes in a gorge below Huascarán.

items.name: Laguna Churup
items.summary: Acclimatisation hike to a glacial lake with a scramble.

items.name: Chavín de Huántar
items.summary: UNESCO temple with underground galleries and the Lanzón idol.

items.name: Pastoruri Glacier
items.summary: Easy walk to a shrinking glacier at 5,000 metres.

items.name: Wilcahuaín ruins
items.summary: Wari-era stone temple above town.

items.name: Huaraz town and Plaza de Armas
items.summary: Town square with mountain views and gear shops.

items.name: Pachamanca
items.summary: Meat and potatoes cooked under hot stones in the earth.

items.name: Andean trout
items.summary: Fresh trout fried or as ceviche.

items.name: Trekker cafés
items.summary: Cafés serving coca tea, pancakes and pizza.

cashTip: Ecuador uses the US dollar. Carry small bills; change for 20s can be hard in small towns.
name: Baños
tagline: Adventure town of waterfalls, hot springs and a volcano swing
summary: Baños is Ecuador's adventure capital, squeezed between the Tungurahua volcano and the Amazon slope. Swing over the valley at the Casa del Árbol, cycle the Route of the Waterfalls to the thundering Pailón del Diablo, raft the Pastaza, and soak in the thermal baths in town.
seasonNote: Rain is possible all year; June to September tends to be drier.
arrival: About 3.5 hours by bus from Quito.
gettingAround: Walk in town; rent a bike or take chivas to the waterfalls.
foodTip: Melcocha taffy, cuy and fresh sugarcane juice.

items.name: Pailón del Diablo
items.summary: Massive waterfall with walkways right beside the torrent.
items.tip: Crawl the tunnel to the ledge.

items.name: Casa del Árbol swing
items.summary: Treehouse swing over the valley facing Tungurahua.
items.expect: Small fee; bus or taxi up.
items.tip: Go early for clear volcano views.

items.name: Route of the Waterfalls
items.summary: Downhill bike ride past waterfalls and cable cars.
items.expect: Rent a bike; ride a truck back.
items.tip: Stop at Manto de la Novia.

items.name: Termas de la Virgen
items.summary: Hot springs fed by the volcano below a waterfall.

items.name: Basílica de Nuestra Señora del Agua Santa
items.wiki: Basílica de Nuestra Señora del Rosario de Agua Santa
items.summary: Pilgrimage church with paintings of miracles.

items.name: Pastaza rafting
items.summary: White-water rafting on class III to IV rapids.

items.name: Melcocha taffy
items.summary: Sugarcane taffy pulled on wooden pegs in shop doorways.

items.name: Cuy
items.summary: Roast guinea pig, an Andean delicacy.

items.name: Sugarcane juice
items.summary: Fresh-pressed cane juice from street stalls.

cashTip: Cards work in restaurants and malls; carry pesos for taxis, street food and salsa bar covers.
name: Cali
summary: Cali is Colombia's salsa capital, a warm city of dance schools, colonial churches and Pacific flavours. Take a salsa class and dance at Tin Tin Deo, wander the colonial San Antonio neighbourhood, climb to Cristo Rey, see the Gato del Río sculptures, and ride a rail cart into the jungle at San Cipriano.
seasonNote: Warm all year; December to February and July to August are drier. The Feria de Cali runs late December.
arrival: Alfonso Bonilla Aragón airport is 30 minutes from the city.
gettingAround: Uber, taxis and the MIO bus.

items.name: Salsa class and clubs
items.summary: Learn Cali-style salsa and dance at famous clubs.

items.name: San Antonio
items.summary: Colonial neighbourhood with a hilltop chapel and cafés.

items.name: Cristo Rey
items.summary: Giant Christ statue above the city.

items.name: El Gato del Río
items.summary: Giant cat sculpture with painted 'girlfriends' along the river.

items.name: La Ermita church
items.summary: Gothic-style church by the river.

items.name: Cali Zoo
items.summary: Colombia's best zoo with native species.

items.name: San Cipriano
items.summary: Jungle village reached by motorbike-powered rail carts.

items.name: Lulada and champús
items.summary: Lulo fruit drink and corn-pineapple champús.

items.name: Galería Alameda
items.summary: Market with Pacific seafood counters.

items.name: Aborrajados
items.summary: Fried ripe plantain stuffed with cheese.
